title: Projects

Problem Gambling

  
  

Description: I have a passion for data visualization and an interest in problem gambling as an under-discussed public health concern. Above is a presentation I created as a part of an independent project to share some concerning problem gambling trends. These figures were made using the Matplotlib library in Python.

title: Projects
text:
Water Quality

  
  

Description: As a part of a 2025 internship with the Chesterfield County Department of Environmental Engineering, I created a presentation highlighting a few key trends related to their catalogue of unanalyzed water quality data. At the end of the internship, I presented these trends to department staff. These figures were made using the Matplotlib library in Python.

title: Christopher Blake Smiley
text:
Email
  

  
  


I am a current PhD student in the Department of Population Health and Quantitative Studies at Case Western Reserve University. My research interests broadly span biostatistical methods, nutritional epidemiology, food system sustainability, cardiovascular health, and graph learning.



In 2026, I graduated from The College of William and Mary with a Bachelor’s of Science in Data Science and a minor in Public Health. Here, I developed a background in both theoretical and applied statistics, computational tools, and public health foundations.
I have worked for the William & Mary Global Research Institute as a research assistant under the direction of Dr. Zach Conrad. As a proud member of the Nutritional Epidemiology and Food Systems Analytics (NEFSA) lab, I gained valuable experience researching food waste and the sustainability impacts of various diets. Here, I honed my research chops and developed a passion for food systems research that I carry with me to this day!
